name: Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial Amritsar
description: A 7-acre public garden memorial preserved to honor the peaceful Indian civilians massacred on Baisakhi, April 13, 1919, by British troops under General Dyer, featuring the preserved Martyr's Well and bullet marks in red brick walls.

name: Bathinda Fort
description: Located in the heart of Bathinda, Punjab, the Bathinda Fort boasts an impressive blend of architectural styles - a perfect amalgamation of Mughal and Rajput structures. Founded by the Bhati Rajputs in the 10th century, this ancient fort has witnessed the rise and fall of numerous dynasties. As you step into this historic complex, you are transported back in time, immersing yourself in the stories etched into its walls.

name: Jang-e-Azadi Memorial Kartarpur
description: Sprawling across 25 acres on the Grand Trunk Road (NH-3) in Kartarpur near Jalandhar, designed by celebrated architect Raj Rewal and opened in 2016, the Jang-e-Azadi Memorial is a world-class experiential museum and memorial complex dedicated to the monumental contributions of Punjabis in the Indian freedom movement, crowned by a majestic 45-meter high circular dome inspired by the Phulkari motif, housing an immersive 3D circular theatre, eight thematic galleries, an outdoor amphitheatre, and a 45-meter flame-shaped Shaheed Smarak tower.

name: Kapurthala
description: Kapurthala, affectionately known as the Paris of Punjab, is a city steeped in a rich princely past, primarily shaped by Maharaja Jagatjit Singh, whose European travels inspired its distinctive Indo-French and Moorish architectural masterpieces. Nestled in the fertile Doaba region of Punjab, the city's geographical setting is characterized by its relatively flat plains, yet it boasts the significant Kanjli Wetland, a vital ecological zone. The local experience is one of stepping back in time, exploring opulent palaces, serene gardens, and experiencing the warm hospitality of Punjabi culture, offering a unique blend of historical grandeur and tranquil natural beauty.

name: Kila Raipur
description: Kila Raipur, a vibrant village nestled in the fertile plains of Punjab's Ludhiana district, is globally celebrated as the host of the annual Kila Raipur Sports Festival, affectionately known as the 'Rural Olympics'. Established in 1933, this iconic event was conceptualized to channel the robust energy and competitive zeal of rural Punjabis, evolving into a grand spectacle of traditional sports and feats of strength. The village itself is characterized by vast, verdant stretches of agricultural fields, predominantly cultivating wheat and paddy, irrigated by an intricate network of canals that underscore the region's agricultural prosperity and natural beauty. Beyond the exhilarating roar of the sports festival, Kila Raipur offers an authentic window into traditional Punjabi rural life. Visitors are welcomed with the legendary warmth of village hospitality, given opportunities to observe time-honored farming practices, and invited to savor the rich, rustic flavors of home-cooked Punjabi cuisine. The cadence of life here is deeply interwoven with the agricultural seasons, celebrating community bonds, diligent hard work, and a profound cultural heritage that reveres strength, sport, and boundless generosity. It is a destination where ancient traditions thrive amidst the serene beauty of rural existence, providing a truly immersive cultural and natural adventure.

name: Gurudwara Dukh Niwaran Sahib
description: Associated with the ninth Sikh Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, who visited Lehal village in 1672 and blessed a pond that miraculously cured villagers of a deadly sickness, now transformed into an immense golden sarovar.

name: Anandpur Sahib
description: Perched on the gentle slopes of the Sivalik Hills, Anandpur Sahib is a tranquil haven steeped in history and spirituality. This sacred Sikh town has been the cradle of Gurbani, the Guru's song, since the 17th century. Anandpur Sahib's breathtaking landscape, dotted with lush forests and rolling hills, is a haven for nature lovers and spiritual seekers alike. The town's rich history, vibrant culture, and stunning natural beauty make it an unforgettable destination for discerning travelers.

name: Guru Tegh Bahadur Sikh Museum (Virasat-e-Khalsa)
description: Designed by world-renowned architect Moshe Safdie at the birthplace of the Khalsa, an awe-inspiring museum complex celebrating 500 years of Sikh history and the martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji with 27 immersive storytelling galleries.

name: Ropar Wetland
description: The Ropar Wetland, also known as the Ropar Lake, is an artificially formed freshwater riverine wetland situated on the Sutlej River in the Rupnagar district of Punjab, India. Created by the construction of headworks for the Bhakra Main Line and Sirhind Canal, this diverse ecosystem was designated a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in 2002 due to its critical role as a habitat for numerous species. It serves as a vital wintering ground for a multitude of migratory birds, including various waterfowl, raptors, and passerines, making it a paradise for birdwatchers and nature enthusiasts. Beyond its ecological significance, the wetland offers a serene escape, blending natural beauty with historical resonance. The surrounding region of Rupnagar (formerly Ropar) holds deep historical roots, being an ancient Harappan site that reveals layers of India's past. Visitors can experience the tranquility of the wetland's waters and lush vegetation, while also connecting with the rich cultural and archaeological heritage of Punjab.

name: Chattbir Zoo (Mahendra Chaudhary Zoological Park)
description: Inaugurated in 1977 on the banks of Ghaggar River, one of Northern India's premier zoological parks spanning 505 acres, famous for open lion and deer safaris, royal Bengal tigers, and Asia's longest walk-in aviary.

name: Fateh Burj (Chappar Chiri War Memorial)
description: Rising majestically to a height of 100 meters (328 feet) on an expansive 20-acre landscaped battlefield memorial in Chappar Chiri near Mohali, inaugurated in November 2011, Fateh Burj ('Victory Tower') is the tallest victory tower in India—surpassing both the Qutub Minar and the Taj Mahal in height—commemorating the historic victory of Sikh commander Baba Banda Singh Bahadur and his Khalsa army over Mughal Governor Wazir Khan in the Battle of Chappar Chiri in May 1710, featuring three tapering octagonal storeys, six memorial earthen mounds (tibbas), and statues of Sikh warrior generals.

name: Gurudwara Singh Shaheedan Sohana
